In the 8th minute, Santiago Lopez turned creator, delivering a precise ball that found Tiziano Perrotta in a dangerous position. After an early period of sparring that saw Max Finkgrafe enter the referee’s book for a rough challenge, the hosts found the breakthrough they were searching for in the 25th minute. A incisive passage of play involving Ibrahim Maza saw the ball find Nathan Tella , who provided a perfectly weighted assist for Patrik Schick . The Czech striker made no mistake, firing home with his left foot to give Leverkusen a vital lead. The goal sparked a wave of pressure from the home side, with Edmond Tapsoba and Jarell Quansah both threatening from set-pieces delivered by the industrious Aleix Garcia . As the first half drew to a close, RB Leipzig struggled to find a rhythm, with their defensive lines forced deeper by Leverkusen ’s fluid movement. The pressure told once more in the 45th minute. Exequiel Palacios orchestrated the move with a key pass to Aleix Garcia , who turned provider for Nathan Tella . The winger showed great composure to strike with his right foot, doubling the advantage just seconds before the interval and leaving the visitors with a mountain to climb in the second period. Schick Dominates the Second Half RB Leipzig manager attempted to spark a comeback with a double substitution at the start of the second half, introducing Castello Lukeba and Brajan Gruda . While the changes provided some renewed energy, including a blocked header from Christoph Baumgartner , the visitors were unable to consistently test the Leverkusen goal. The hosts remained dangerous on the break, with Alejandro Grimaldo nearly adding a third from a direct free kick that whistled just wide of the target. In the 76th minute, the game was effectively put beyond doubt. Ibrahim Maza , a constant thorn in the side of the Leipzig defense, registered his second assist of the match by finding Patrik Schick . The striker once again utilized his clinical left foot to find the back of the net, marking his second goal of the afternoon. Leipzig did manage to pull one back shortly after in the 80th minute when Brajan Gruda whipped in a cross for Christoph Baumgartner to head home, but it proved to be a mere consolation as the hosts maintained their composure. VAR Confirmation and Hat-trick Heroics The closing stages were marred by a flurry of yellow cards for Christoph Baumgartner and Malik Tillman as frustrations boiled over for the visitors, but the headlines belonged solely to Patrik Schick . In the 89th minute, Alejandro Grimaldo delivered a precise ball into the box for Schick to sweep home. While the linesman initially raised his flag, a lengthy VAR review followed. The tension in the stadium was palpable until the referee pointed to the center spot, confirming the goal and completing a magnificent hat-trick for the Leverkusen talisman. Schick was substituted in the final moments to a standing ovation, replaced by Christian Kofane as the game entered four minutes of stoppage time. With 55% of the possession and a clear edge in offensive quality, Bayer Leverkusen comfortably saw out the remaining seconds. The final whistle confirmed a comprehensive victory for the hosts, who celebrated a clinical performance that showcased their credentials as one of the league's most formidable attacking units.

Heidenheim’s Early Blitz Stuns the Allianz Despite Bayern Munich dominating the early ball possession, it was 1. FC Heidenheim who displayed a masterclass in efficiency during the opening half-hour. The visitors broke the deadlock in the 22nd minute when Marnon-Thomas Busch provided a pinpoint delivery for Budu Zivzivadze , who made no mistake with a composed left-footed finish to give the underdogs a shock lead. The goal appeared to rattle the hosts, and before Bayern could find their rhythm, Heidenheim struck again. In the 31st minute, Busch was once again the architect, setting up Eren Dinkci for a simple tap-in that left the home support in a state of disbelief. Bayern Munich attempted to respond through Hiroki Ito , whose ambitious effort from distance whistled just wide of the post. The pressure from the Bavarian giants was constant, but a lack of clinical finishing in the final third seemed destined to haunt them as the first half drew to a close. However, the momentum shifted just before the interval when Leon Goretzka stepped up to a direct free kick in the 44th minute. The midfielder unleashed a spectacular right-footed strike that curled into the back of the net, giving Bayern a vital lifeline and cutting the deficit to 2-1 heading into the dressing rooms. Tactical Overhaul and the Goretzka Double Recognizing the need for a spark, Bayern manager made a daring quadruple substitution at the start of the second half. Joshua Kimmich , Luis Diaz , Michael Olise , and the prolific Harry Kane were all introduced to the fray, signaling a total offensive commitment. The impact was almost immediate as the hosts pinned Heidenheim back into their own box. In the 56th minute, Min-Jae Kim thought he had equalized, only to see his goal-bound effort heroically cleared off the line by the retreating defense. Undeterred, Bayern found their second goal just a minute later. In the 57th minute, Michael Olise began his influential second-half cameo by swinging in a corner that found Leon Goretzka . The German international remained composed to slot home his second of the match with his right foot, bringing the scores level at 2-2. With over half an hour remaining and 75% of the possession, it seemed only a matter of time before the record champions would complete the comeback and take all three points. Stoppage Time Drama and Olise’s Redemption Football rarely follows a predictable script, and Heidenheim proved their resilience in the 76th minute. Against the run of play, Arijon Ibrahimovic —who had been a creative force for the visitors—found Budu Zivzivadze in the area. The forward made no mistake, firing home his second goal of the afternoon to restore Heidenheim 's lead. Bayern threw everything forward in response, with Luis Diaz coming agonizingly close from the edge of the box, but a series of yellow cards for Jonathan Tah and Konrad Laimer highlighted the growing frustration within the home ranks. As the match entered ten minutes of added time, the tension reached a breaking point. Heidenheim 's Jonas Foehrenbach required lengthy medical treatment as the visitors desperately tried to hold onto their narrow advantage. Marnon-Thomas Busch received a late booking for a cynical foul, and it appeared the visitors might survive the onslaught. However, in the 100th minute, Alphonso Davies found space to provide one final cross for Michael Olise . The French winger controlled the ball outside the box and unleashed a stunning right-footed strike that beat the keeper, securing a dramatic 3-3 draw in the dying seconds of a classic Bundesliga encounter.
